bull_bear.body:
- Owns a scarce, irreplaceable waterfront estate at Colaba in south Mumbai that is used as a shooting location - a location asset that cannot be replicated by competitors
- Asset-light cost base with only 4 permanent employees on roll, so incremental revenue from letting space converts strongly into operating profit
- Reconstructed sea-retaining wall and newly concreted 22,000 sq ft area have added usable, revenue-generating area to the same site
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-asset, single-segment concentration — The Company operates in one segment only - income from rendering services by providing space for film shooting, TV serials and advertisements - and all of that activity sits on one property at Colaba, Mumbai. Any disruption to that single site or to demand from film/TV/advertising producers removes essentially all revenue, with no other business or location to absorb it. (Segment note read in the related-party bundle; property narrative in the MD&A.)
- Unresolved Supreme Court litigation blocking development of the Colaba property — The Company's Special Leave Petition before the Supreme Court, challenging the Bombay High Court order on the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai's refusal to approve its building plans, could not be concluded during the year because the Bench composition changed. Until the matter is finally heard, the Company cannot proceed with approved development of its principal asset, and the outcome is outside its control.
- Defence-establishment objections constraining building approvals — The municipal refusal to approve the Company's plans was primarily on account of objections raised by the Indian Navy. A structural planning constraint arising from an adjacent defence establishment is not something the Company can negotiate away commercially, and it may persist regardless of how the litigation is decided.
- Coastal and extreme-weather exposure to the sea-retaining wall and platform — In May 2021 cyclone Taukte severely damaged part of the sea-retaining wall on the south-east side of the property, washing away part of the platform behind it and damaging structures. The Company completed the repairs and refilled approximately 22,000 sq ft, but the asset remains a seafront property exposed to recurrence of the same event.
- Repair obligation for the Mumbai Port Trust sea wall falls on the Company — MbPT did not carry out the required repairs and has taken the stand that it will not repair or reconstruct its sea-retaining wall/platform, with no objection to the Company doing so at the Company's own cost. A cost that properly belongs to a third party therefore becomes an open-ended call on the Company's own funds, with no quantum stated.
- Accumulated losses and a very small revenue base — The Company carries a large accumulated loss forward to the balance sheet and returned to profit only in the year under review after a loss in the prior year, on a revenue base measured in the low hundreds of lakhs. That leaves minimal buffer to absorb a downturn, a legal setback or an unplanned repair to the sea wall.
- Extreme key-person dependence on a four-person organisation — The Company has 4 (four) permanent employees on roll, and during the year the combined Company Secretary/Compliance Officer/CFO resigned and was replaced by two separate appointees in November 2025. Continuity of operations, compliance and institutional knowledge rests on a handful of individuals.
- Reduced corporate-governance obligations because of small size — Because paid-up equity capital does not exceed Rs. 10 crore and net worth does not exceed Rs. 25 crore, the corporate-governance provisions of Regulations 17 to 27 and Schedule V of the SEBI Listing Regulations are not applicable to the Company. The Company has constituted the Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship and Risk Management Committees voluntarily, so the governance safeguards minority shareholders rely on are self-imposed rather than mandatory - and the Risk Management Committee met only once during FY26.

business.body: The Company operates a single line of business: rendering services by providing space for film shooting, TV serials and advertisements at its property at Colaba, Mumbai. It has no manufacturing operations and is run by a very small on-roll team, with revenue driven by upgrading the site's infrastructure and reaching new customer segments while retaining existing ones. Following cyclone Taukte damage in May 2021, the Company completed repairs and reconstruction of its sea-retaining wall and refilled and concrete-surfaced the washed-out area, which has started generating revenue.

outlook.body:
- Grow revenue from services by upgrading the Colaba property's infrastructure through substantial investment, an effort management says it has sustained over the last few years
- Broaden the customer base by reaching out to new customer segments while maintaining focus on existing ones
- Carry out necessary repairs and renovations to certain structures on the property so a broader range of customer segments can be attracted and revenue potential enhanced

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TCI Industries has no manufacturing capex programme; its expansion is confined to upgrading its single property at Colaba, Mumbai. After cyclone Taukte damaged part of the sea-retaining wall on the south-east side of the property in May 2021, the Company completed repairs and reconstruction of the wall and filled up the washed-out area, surface-finishing the entire approximately 22,000 sq ft in concrete, and that area has started generating revenue (Board's Report; reaches this bundle cross-bundle from the governance routing). Mumbai Port Trust has declined to repair or reconstruct its own sea-retaining wall/platform and has stated it has no objection to the Company carrying out that work at the Company's own cost, so any further wall works remain a Company-funded obligation. Looking ahead, management says it plans to further improve infrastructure and carry out necessary repairs and renovations to certain structures on the property to attract a broader range of customer segments and enhance revenue potential. No project timeline, no commissioning date and no rupee quantum is stated for any of this work.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management attributes the improved performance during the year primarily to a significant increase in revenue from operations, which it says reflects strengthening business operations and sustained business momentum
- Revenue is expected to be driven by continued infrastructure upgrades to the property plus outreach to new customer segments alongside the existing ones
- The approximately 22,000 sq ft washed-out area, refilled and surface-finished in concrete after the sea-retaining wall reconstruction, has started generating revenue (cross-bundle: stated in the Board's Report/governance bundle)
- Management states the Company remains optimistic about achieving better results in the current year and the near future, given the developments and ongoing efforts described
- The Company operates in a single segment - income from rendering services by providing space for film shooting, TV serials and advertisements - so demand is tied entirely to that end market (cross-bundle: Note 33 Segment Information, seen in the governance/related-party bundle)
